newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestine Telecommunications Co gets licence.
newsitem.headline: Palestine Telecommunications Co gets licence.

text.p: The Palestinian Ministry of Post and Telecommunications has awarded a licence to the Palestine Telecommunications Company (PALTEL) to provide telecommunications services in self-ruled areas, PALTEL said on Sunday.
The licence agreement was signed in Gaza, less than a month after a public offering in PALTEL that closed nearly five times oversubscribed, the company said in a statement.
Some 7,000 private investors have taken a stake in PALTEL, founded by a group of Palestinian private investors, the statement said.

"Our plans are to bring the number of customers to 250,000 in three years...in the long term, the company will strive to create an entirely independent public communications network in Palestine," the statement quoted PALTEL director general Mohammad Mustafa as saying at the signing ceremony.
Israel's state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecommunications company still provides the international lines used in the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Mustaafa said PALTEL would introduce data communications, public payphones, paging services, satellite communications and the Internet to self-ruled parts of the West Bank and Gaza.
"We are ready to begin procuring a GSM public cellular telephone network which will be the first-ever Palestinian mobile network," Mustafa was quoted as saying.
The company plans to take over operations from the Palestinian Ministry of Post and Telecommunications within weeks.
